title: Try to remember the history of this musical!! #broadway #musicaltheat...
transcript: so the longest running musical of all time is aiming for Broadway with a queer reimagining but it's come to my attention that some of you don't know enough about one of my favorite musicals ever. welcome to another episode of Overthinking Theatre Throwback where I do retrospectives on recent theatre history. although in this case it's sort of recent and sort of not because let's talk about their insanely long record-breaking run in 2017 The Fantasticks closed off Broadway after more than 50 years in New York…sorta… that production was technically a revival directed by one of the show's writers, Tom Jones which opened only about 4 1/2 years after the original closed but the original ran for almost 42 years so even excluding the revival's very impressive 11 year run The Fantasticks still holds the record for the longest running musical of all time among other superlatives But because of the circumstances and the timing of the revival sometimes people like to sneakily lump them together and talk about the combined total 21,552 performances in New York over the course of 57 years in that time it starred many well known artists including Jerry Orbach and the original cast Liza Minelli as a replacement all the way to former teen pop star Aaron Carter but what about the musical itself? well part of the reason it was able to run so long is that it's conceived for a very bare bones staging with a kind of DIY theatre troupe aesthetic. inspired by an 1894 play by Edmond Rostand (best known for Cyrano de Bergerac) The Fantasticks tells the story of a boy and a girl (originally) who overcome ostensibly forbidden love in Act 1 only to be disillusioned by some harsher realities in Act 2 it kinda did the into the Woods thing before into the Woods did it it was actually my first ever off Broadway show I saw it kind of on a whim in 2011 and I was just so immediately enchanted by its tender poeticism and its deceptively clever structure but also deeply moved by its profound insights on life and love. Cut to just last week, it was announced that a new revival is aiming for Broadway this time reimagined as a love story between two boys this reimagining was originally conceived by Michael Lluberes for a Michigan premiere in 2022 though it was Tom Jones himself who implemented the rewrites I will say for myself I'm excited to see any version of this musical again and to see how it does or doesn't play differently as a gay love story but I am cautiously intrigued by the announcement that their end goal is Broadway it would be the first Broadway production of a musical that's been strongly associated with its intimacy and sparse staging even this specific revision of the material has been produced a few times already but I believe only in pretty small venues having said that this would be a new production directed by Christopher Gattelli who, as a choreographer, might find his own ways to fill out the Broadway-sized space so we'll see! or at least I hope so I always take these announcements with a grain of salt but I hope it does come to fruition
classificationReason: Historical retrospective about The Fantasticks and news of an upcoming queer reimagining heading to Broadway. The Fantasticks is not in the provided list, and there is no first-hand review of a listed production.
